good, but theres some annoying stuff. this drivers ed app is ok and i like how it keeps track of my progress by hour, percentage, and how many levels completed. ex: level 8 section 3 is 63% complete and i have an estimate of 11 hours remaining. 

however, there are some "bugs" that are mildly annoying or just somewhat ridiculous placement. 
my first complaint would be the "next" button when it goes from a text to a mini quiz. once you finish reading the text, you click the arrow button and find yourself at some sort of quiz. the design flaw is that whenever pressing fast forward, i sometimes accidentally press next before i even read the text. so i am stuck in a quiz that i never got the chance to study for. then have to guess and go back to actually read the passage. if this repeats too much then the quizzes are inevitably useless and arent helping. i suggest to have some sort of pop up or sign that alerts the student that theres something next so they are alert. i also recommend putting the "next" button elsewhere (away from the fast forward button) or have a question pop up to ask the student if they have finished reading because there will be a question next. 
my second complaint is mainly on mobile devices. when theres a set of instructions that we are told to put in order, the press and hold button is to the right and right next to the "scrolling" line. when trying to press and hold to move an instruction, it instead can leave you scrolling up or down. i have wasted 10 minutes doing this task and i had to eventually switch to a laptop where there is no scrolling feature to bother me. i suggest either making the whole sentence able to press and hold so it can be moved, change it to the left, or a numbering system instead.

Disappointing, Dangerous, Tedious, and Expensive.. If I could’ve rated this course a 0 I would. I chose Aceable because I read online that it should be the ‘best overall’ for time, difficulty, and depth, but this was very inaccurate. 

First, this course does NOT prepare you for the exams. I took the full course, and I took multiple practice exams for the knowledge test and failed because it gave silly questions and responses such as ‘traffic in the neighboring lane is ___ b) stupid (but don’t tell them) d) going kinda fast’ This is not realistic to the real test, and WON’T help you. 

Next, and MOST importantly, this course is genuinely dangerous. On the lesson, ‘Animal Collisions cont,’ the course suggests that it may be safer to crash into an elephant rather than swerving. On the lesson, ‘Not a Place to Stop,’ the course suggests that if your car is stuck on railroad tracks and you don’t think a train is coming, you should try to push the car out of the tracks. REALLY?

Lastly, the course is not at all information dense, rather, it’s full of unnecessary information and ‘#aceable’ NONSENSE. A better course would be straight to the point and the points that you need to know. 

And then of course, it’s CRAZY expensive. I bought it for $35 and $5 a month, but online I’m reading that it’s $50!! Not worth the price.

reviews.text: Great Course, little weird sometimes. The functionality works great, it’s easy and quick to use. Customer service is really amazing too. My only real problem is that the videos and some of the material is a little- wack. It feels like it was written by some 60 year old trying to “be relatable for the kids” but just embarrassing everybody in the process. I kid you not some of these videos are so outlandish and weird that it’s impossible to take in the information being presented in them, because they’re so childish you can’t focus on the actual material. The written material and the videos included that weren’t produced by Aceable are all great. However, some of the videos just really mess it up. However, there are other really useful ones. Some videos involving real world scenarios (such as intersections, skids, etc) are actually really helpful. They’re simply animated, which makes it a lot easier to digest and understand than an actual video. They’re also short and each video is relevant to a subject. None of them are lectures, which I appreciate. Granted, none of this really matters considering it’s an incredibly easy and practical way to complete drivers ed. From what Ive done so far, I’m relatively sure you can complete it in well under 30 hours if you’re a quick reader and understand the concepts. If the purpose of this course was JUST to learn how to drive (no DMV certificate involved), I would probably have given it 3 stars. However, the practicality and ease that this affords a student driver definitely makes it worth it.
